v06.welcome: Make this workspace work for you
v06.presentationOnly: These choices change guidance and presentation. They never change project data, scientific meaning or permissions.
v06.role.question: What best describes your work?
v06.experience.question: How comfortable are you with biodiversity data tools?
v06.beginnerExplanation: Start with explanations, use ordinary research terminology, or expose technical tools. You can change this at any time.
v06.guidanceNotMandate: These are suggested tasks, not a scientifically mandatory order. Unknown and intentionally unresolved are valid outcomes.
v06.noRecommendations: No further suggestions in this analysis. Review validation and export requirements before sharing.
v06.sampleCoverage: Sampled {sampled} of {total} rows. Suggestions describe this sample; validation and export checks remain separate.
v06.noAutomaticMeaning: No scientific meanings, relationships, units, dates or coordinate systems were assigned automatically.
v06.analyzing: Reading local working annotations and analyzing the project…
v06.translationExplanation: Turn old or inconsistent data into a clearer, reusable structure. Original files stay intact. Mechanical repairs are previewed; scientific interpretation stays under your control.
v06.queueExplanation: Review what needs attention across your project. Record what you investigated, including decisions that must remain unresolved.
v06.statusNotice: This is a suggestion, not an evidence-confirmed interpretation. Heuristic confidence:
v06.relationshipCounts: {matched} sampled references match; {orphans} sampled references have no match. This does not establish a scientific relationship.
v06.reviewExplanation: Accepting or rejecting a suggestion records your review only. It does not confirm scientific meaning or transform data. Use the relevant tool and surviving evidence for interpretation. Explain what you investigated.
v06.repairCount: {count} values would change. Only surrounding whitespace is removed. Inspect the preview and explain your decision before applying.
v06.wholeProject: Original fields → recorded understanding → possible standard representation
v06.noMatchingIssues: No suggestions match this filter. This does not certify the dataset’s scientific quality.
v06.reviewPageLimit: Only the first 100 suggestions are displayed. Filter by category to review others; the complete analysis remains available.
v06.privateNotes: Working notes and bookmarks are local annotations, separate from scientific metadata. They are not automatically included in scientific exports. Download them separately for backup.
v06.why.name: The field name resembles a common research term. This name-based rule cannot establish scientific meaning, even when values look plausible.
v06.why.unknown: No defensible field meaning was found. Surviving documentation may help. Leaving this unknown is safer than guessing.
v06.why.conflict: The recorded interpretation is conflicting. Keep competing evidence visible rather than choosing automatically.
v06.why.mapping: A confirmed field definition has no recorded standard mapping. The name suggests this candidate; check the actual meaning and table structure first.
v06.why.trim: Some sampled values contain surrounding whitespace. A complete-table preview is required before applying this mechanical repair.
v06.why.missing: These literal tokens resemble missing-value conventions. They might also be real measurements or codes. Do not convert without evidence.
v06.why.date: The sampled dates permit both day-first and month-first readings. Two-digit years also need evidence about the century. Workbench will not choose automatically.
v06.why.unit: The column-name suffix resembles a unit. It is an inference from the name, not confirmed measurement context.
v06.why.coordinate: The field name resembles a coordinate axis. The datum and coordinate reference system remain unknown unless documented.
v06.why.taxonomy: This field may record a taxon name or code. Historical names remain literal; current-name lookup requires explicit review and provenance.
v06.why.relationship: Two fields have matching normalized names and overlapping sampled values. Review parent uniqueness, cardinality, unmatched references and the real scientific connection.
v06.why.codebook: The table name resembles a codebook. Its first two fields are shown as candidate codes and meanings; this is not a confirmed dictionary. Conflicting definitions remain visible.
v06.why.metadata: Project context is missing or unconfirmed. Describe only what surviving evidence can support.
v06.why.privacy: Coordinate fields may expose sensitive locations. Review public-export handling before sharing; this does not establish that the locations are sensitive.
v06.kind.mapping: Review a possible standard mapping for {field}
v06.kind.taxonomy: Review historical taxon names or codes in {field}
v06.settings.explanation: Settings change how Workbench behaves. They do not change the scientific contents of your project.
v06.settings.local: Local-only. Optional external lookups require explicit opt-in; this profile does not enable any network service.
v06.settings.autosave: Committed changes are saved on this computer. Unsaved forms are recovery drafts. Keep an independent portable backup; local working annotations have a separate download.
v06.settings.recovery: Open Recovery Center to inspect committed revisions, drafts and snapshots. Recovery is separate from an independent backup.
v06.settings.import: Parsing preferences are suggestions. Review encoding, delimiter and table structure before interpreting a legacy file.
v06.settings.validation: Display preferences never weaken validation or export gates. Hidden errors still block applicable standards exports.
v06.settings.large: Most users do not need to change these settings. Large CSV investigations use bounded disk-backed processing.
v06.settings.advanced: Inspect exact schemas and installed standard providers in Standards Center. A structural check is not scientific certification.
v06.settings.about: Application {version} · project schema 3 · local-first biodiversity data rescue. Read the included privacy, security and license documentation.
v06.helpUnknown: Unknown is a valid result. Workbench never requires you to invent meaning to finish a review.
v06.importLimits: Normal-project import: up to 100 files, 50 MiB total, 20 MiB per file. Use Large CSV for bigger investigations.
v06.importInspecting: Inspecting files locally. Nothing has been changed.
v06.nothingChanged: Nothing has been changed. Review the discovery below before preserving these files in your project. Classification is tentative; original bytes are retained.
v06.importCategory.documents: Documents that may explain the data
v06.importCategory.preserved: Files preserved without a full inspection
v06.preserveUninterpreted: Original bytes preserved without inventing a structure
v06.importNeedsReview: Inspection needs review; the original file will still be retained.
v06.optionalTitle: Optional project title · leave blank to keep the current title
v06.importProjectChanged: The selected project changed during discovery. Cancel and start again to avoid importing into the wrong project.
v06.helpExplanation: Find plain-language explanations. Technical terms describe the same scientific model, whichever workspace profile you use.
v06.tagsExplanation: Tags help organize Project Hub. They are working annotations and are not scientific metadata.
v06.why.validation: A local check found a record, structure or documentation problem. Review the underlying finding; resolving a review annotation does not waive the validation rule.
v06.help.Project: This is your project’s starting point. Review what you have, what remains unknown, and a suggested next task. Suggestions do not certify scientific quality.
v06.help.Sources: Original files are the retained evidence. Check their digital fingerprints and lengths before interpreting working copies.
v06.help.Inspect: Explore literal recorded values and their patterns. A plausible pattern can suggest a meaning, but it cannot confirm one.
v06.help.Metadata: Describe the research and field meanings using surviving evidence. Unknown and conflicting interpretations are valid.
v06.help.Relationships: Different tables may describe surveys, observations or specimens. Review identifiers and unmatched references before connecting them.
v06.help.Evidence: Record why you believe something about an old dataset. Keep competing documents and interpretations visible.
v06.help.Repair: Preview a confirmed correction, explain why it is justified, then apply it to working data. Original files remain unchanged.
v06.help.Review queue: Track what you investigated. Intentionally unresolved means a review could not recover a defensible answer; it is different from never reviewed.
v06.help.Translate & standardize: Review candidate meanings, codebooks, units and standard terms. Formatting repairs and scientific interpretation require different decisions.
v06.help.Map to Standards: Map a confirmed field meaning to a supported standard term. A matching column name alone is not enough.
v06.help.Validate: Check structure and recorded conventions. Errors remain active even if a review card or filter hides them.
v06.help.Export: Prepare a reusable or preservation package. Review rights, sensitive locations, validation and the package inventory before sharing.
v06.help.Audit / Report: Follow the provenance of changes and export a rescue summary. Undo and redo add history rather than erasing it.
v06.help.Snapshots: A checkpoint helps recover a local state. It is not an independent backup of the computer.
v06.help.Storage & Recovery: Inspect saved revisions, drafts and recovery checkpoints. Keep a separate portable backup for independent protection.
v06.help.Large CSV: Investigate large files using disk-backed pages and bounded processing. Large mode has its own documented limits.
v06.help.Standards validation: Check an uploaded package against the installed local adapters. Coverage and unavailable dependencies remain explicit.
v06.help.DwC-DP preparation: Prepare explicit fields and tables for a Darwin Core review package. A draft review provider is not a ratified conformance certificate.
v06.help.Standards Center: See which standard versions and checks are actually installed. No remote services run automatically.
v06.help.Saved for later: Keep private working notes and bookmarks separately from scientific metadata. Download them separately when backing up.
v06.help.Settings: Change presentation, language and local behavior. These controls never change scientific meanings.
v06.help.Help: Look up concepts and reopen the product tour or fictional guided rescue. Learning should not require guessing a scientific answer.
v06.help.About: Inspect the application identity, privacy boundary and acknowledged standard versions.
v06.integrityVerified: Current retained originals match their recorded checksums and byte lengths. Keep an independent backup.
v06.integrityFailed: An original-file checksum or byte length does not match. Investigate source integrity before interpreting or exporting the data.
v06.error.0: Restore the project before changing working annotations.
v06.error.1: WORKSPACE_STATE_STALE: reload the working annotations before saving.
v06.error.2: Working annotations exceed the 1 MiB limit; export a local copy before adding more.
v06.error.4: Explain this review decision; unknown remains a valid answer.
v06.error.7: Working annotation entries require stable IDs.
v06.error.9: Working annotation lists are limited to 1,000 entries.
v06.recommendations: Show suggested next steps on Overview
v06.glossary.occurrence.definition: A record that an organism or group of organisms was observed at a place and time. A non-detection needs separate survey-effort context.
v06.glossary.event.definition: A survey, sampling visit or other activity with a place, time and method. An event may have many observations or no detections.
v06.glossary.field.definition: One column describing an attribute of each record. Its name alone does not establish its meaning or units.
v06.glossary.table.definition: Records organized into rows and fields. Document what one row represents before combining tables.
v06.glossary.inference.definition: An interpretation suggested by observations or context. It remains uncertain until someone reviews supporting evidence.
v06.glossary.validation.definition: Checks against declared rules that find problems needing review. Passing checks does not prove scientific correctness.
v06.glossary.darwinCore.definition: Shared terms for describing biodiversity observations and related information. A mapping needs a documented field meaning.
v06.glossary.dwcdp.definition: Darwin Core Data Package: a structured package of related biodiversity tables and their descriptions. The bundled review provider is unratified.
v06.glossary.eml.definition: Ecological Metadata Language: an open XML format describing ecological datasets, methods, fields and people.
v06.glossary.rocrate.definition: A linked JSON-LD description of files, their origins and research context. Workbench performs scoped graph and payload checks.
v06.glossary.camtrap.definition: Camera Trap Data Package: a format linking camera deployments, media and observations with package metadata.
v06.glossary.taxon.definition: A named biological group, such as a species. A name or abbreviation requires evidence before assigning an authoritative identity.
v06.glossary.codebook.definition: A document or lookup table explaining recorded codes. Conflicting definitions should remain visible rather than being silently combined.
v06.glossary.missing.definition: A value that is unavailable or unrecorded. Blank, zero, non-detection and sentinel codes can have different scientific meanings.
v06.glossary.normalization.definition: A documented change to represent values consistently. Formatting changes and scientific interpretations require different kinds of review.
